answer: The atlas of trusted travelers holds exactly one real person per entry: a NEXUS card needs an in-person interview at a joint US-Canada enrollment center, fingerprints and an iris scan checked against both countries' watchlists, for $50 and five years of validity. A farm buying 1,000 identities pays $50,000 plus 1,000 face-to-face appearances, and the ferrous iris scanner is unforgiving — one mismatched scan flags the whole batch, freezing every linked identity while the kernel of the enrollment record is re-verified against the original biometrics.
